title: Review: Cell potential under nonstandard conditions (AP); Quantitative electrolysis (Faraday); Practical techniques and uncertainties
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: PR01a#t1 term and clue written for the game; RX08#t4 term and clue written for the game; PR01b#t2 term and clue written for the game; RX10#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: PR01a#N.13, PR01b#N.9, RX08#N.8, RX10#N.6, PR01a#N.12, RX08#N.6, RX10#N.10, PR01a#N.10, RX08#N.7, RX10#N.3, RX08#N.3, RX08#N.9. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Random error
items.clue: Makes readings scatter either way; repeats and a mean reduce its effect.

items.label: Faraday constant
items.clue: The value 96,485 C/mol e⁻, used to turn coulombs into moles of electrons.

items.label: Hazard
items.clue: Something that could cause harm, such as a corrosive or flammable substance.

items.label: Equilibrium
items.clue: State reached when Q = K and E = 0, with no net electron flow: a dead battery.

questions.stem: A student mixes two solutions in a polystyrene cup to find an enthalpy of reaction. The thermometer has an uncertainty of ±0.5 °C per reading, and the temperature rises by only about 4 °C. Which change would most reduce the relative uncertainty in the temperature change, ΔT? -

options.text: Use larger volumes of the same two solutions.
Use more concentrated solutions, keeping the same volumes.
Start with both solutions at a higher temperature.
Record each temperature to two decimal places.

questions.explanation: More reacts in the same volume, so ΔT is larger (e.g. about 20 °C). The ±1.0 °C uncertainty in ΔT is then about 5% instead of 25%.

questions.stem: A student must heat a reaction mixture containing ethanol (highly flammable, boiling point 78 °C) for 30 minutes. Which plan best controls the risk?

options.text: Heat it over a Bunsen burner on a low flame, in a fume cupboard.
Heat it over a Bunsen burner, wearing gloves and eye protection.
Heat it under reflux, using a water bath or an electric heater.
Heat it in an open beaker so that the vapour can escape.

questions.explanation: No naked flame, and the condenser returns ethanol vapour to the flask, so little escapes.

questions.stem: A constant current deposits 0.010 mol of Ag(s) from a solution containing Ag⁺(aq) in 30 minutes. The same current is then passed through a solution containing Au³⁺(aq). How long does it take to deposit 0.010 mol of Au(s)?

options.text: 30 min
10 min
55 min
90 min

questions.explanation: Au³⁺ gains 3 electrons, Ag⁺ gains 1. Three times the charge at the same current takes three times as long.

questions.stem: A galvanic cell based on Zn(s) + Cu²⁺(aq) → Zn²⁺(aq) + Cu(s) is operating at 25°C. Solid Cu(NO₃)₂ is dissolved in the copper half-cell, increasing [Cu²⁺], and the measured cell potential increases. Which explanation of the increase is correct?

options.text: The cell's equilibrium shifts toward products, as Le Châtelier's principle predicts
More ions are present in solution, so more charge carriers raise the potential
E° for the cell increases, because the reactant ion is now more concentrated
Q decreases, so the cell is farther from equilibrium, and its driving force is greater

questions.explanation: Q = [Zn²⁺]/[Cu²⁺] falls when [Cu²⁺] increases, moving the cell farther from equilibrium (Q = K). The cell potential measures this driving force, so it increases.

questions.stem: A student plots the volume of gas collected against time. The best-fit line is straight, but does not pass through the origin. It passes through (10 s, 14 mL) and (50 s, 62 mL). What is the slope, in mL/s?
questions.explanation: (62 − 14) ÷ (50 − 10) = 48 ÷ 40 = 1.2. The line meets the y-axis at 2 cm³, so one point alone gives the wrong answer.

questions.stem: A student electroplates zinc onto a cathode from ZnSO₄(aq). During the experiment the mass of the cathode increases by 0.327 g. What quantity of charge passed through the cell? (F = 96,485 C/mol e⁻.)

A concentration cell is made from two silver electrodes. The left electrode dips into 0.0010 M AgNO₃(aq) and the right into 0.10 M AgNO₃(aq), with a salt bridge between them. The cell is connected to a small motor and left to run. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Electrons flow from right to left, and E stays constant until the silver ions on the right are used up.
Electrons flow from left to right, and E falls toward zero as the two concentrations become closer.
No electrons flow, because E° is zero when both electrodes are made of silver.
Electrons flow from left to right, and E rises as the cell runs, because Q increases.

questions.stem: A student dissolves 2.5 g of NaCl (molar mass 58.5 g/mol) in water and makes the solution up to 250.0 mL. Which value of the molarity, in M, is given to the appropriate number of significant figures?
questions.explanation: 2.5 ÷ 58.5 ÷ 0.2500 = 0.1709… The mass has only 2 significant figures, so the answer has 2: 0.17.

questions.stem: A student electroplates nickel onto a cathode from NiSO₄(aq), using a constant current of 2.50 A. For how long must the current pass to increase the mass of the cathode by 2.348 g? (F = 96,485 C/mol e⁻.)

options.text: 25.7 min
12.9 min
51.5 min
19.5 min

questions.stem: A galvanic cell based on the reaction Zn(s) + Cu²⁺(aq) → Zn²⁺(aq) + Cu(s) is connected to a light bulb and allowed to operate at constant temperature. How does the cell potential change as the cell operates, and why?

options.text: It decreases, because Q rises as Zn²⁺ forms and Cu²⁺ is used up, nearing equilibrium
It stays the same, because the potential is fixed by the two half-reactions in the cell
It decreases, because the zinc electrode becomes smaller as zinc atoms are oxidized
It stays the same until the Cu²⁺ ions are used up, and it then falls to zero

questions.stem: A steel spoon is nickel-plated, using a nickel anode in NiSO₄(aq). Which pair of half-equations is correct?

options.text: Cathode: Ni(s) → Ni²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻. Anode: Ni²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ → Ni(s).
Cathode: Ni²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ → Ni(s). Anode: 2H₂O(l) → O₂(g) + 4H⁺(aq) + 4e⁻.
Cathode: Ni²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ → Ni(s). Anode: Ni(s) → Ni²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻.
Cathode: 2H₂O(l) + 2e⁻ → H₂(g) + 2OH⁻(aq). Anode: Ni(s) → Ni²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻.

questions.explanation: Nickel is deposited on the spoon (cathode) and the nickel anode dissolves. 2 electrons gained, 2 lost.

questions.stem: A spoon is silver-plated using a silver anode in AgNO₃(aq). A current of 0.150 A passes for 20.0 min. What mass of silver is lost from the anode? (F = 96,485 C/mol e⁻; Ag = 107.87 g/mol)

options.text: 0 g, because only the spoon changes mass
